claims.text: NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened an Audit Query numbered AQ26002 into Tesla's Cybercab certification.
claims.quote:
OFFICE OF DEFECTS INVESTIGATION
Investigation: AQ26002
claims.document: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation, opening resume for Audit Query AQ26002

claims.text: The audit query was opened on September 3rd, 2026.
claims.quote:
Investigation: AQ26002
Prompted By: Public Information
Date Opened: 09/03/2026
claims.document: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation, opening resume for Audit Query AQ26002

claims.text: The action NHTSA took is an Open Audit Query rather than a defect investigation or a recall.
claims.quote: Action: Open Audit Query (AQ)
claims.document: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation, opening resume for Audit Query AQ26002

claims.text: The audit query names Tesla, Inc. as the manufacturer and Tesla Cybercab vehicles as the products under examination.
claims.quote:
Manufacturer: Tesla, Inc.
Products: Tesla Cybercab vehicles
claims.document: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation, opening resume for Audit Query AQ26002

claims.text: The audit query covers an estimated population of 1,000 vehicles.
claims.quote: Population: 1,000 (Estimated)
claims.document: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation, opening resume for Audit Query AQ26002

claims.text: NHTSA states the purpose of the audit as an examination of the process and technical data Tesla relied on when certifying the Cybercab.
claims.quote: Problem Description: Examination of the process and technical data on which Tesla relied when certifying the Cybercab and related issues.
claims.document: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation, opening resume for Audit Query AQ26002

claims.text: Tesla began commercial deployment of a small number of Cybercab vehicles in Austin, Texas on September 3rd, 2026.
claims.quote: On September 3, 2026, Tesla began commercial deployment with a small number of its Cybercab vehicles in Austin, Texas.
claims.document: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation, opening resume for Audit Query AQ26002

claims.text: Tesla told NHTSA that it had certified those Cybercab vehicles as compliant with all applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards.
claims.quote: Tesla notified the Agency that it certified those Cybercab vehicles as compliant with all applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS).
claims.document: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation, opening resume for Audit Query AQ26002

claims.text: Tesla also told NHTSA it plans to expand the deployment gradually to more vehicles and more locations.
claims.quote: Tesla also notified the Agency that it plans to gradually expand commercial deployment of the Cybercab to include additional vehicles and locations.
claims.document: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation, opening resume for Audit Query AQ26002

claims.text: NHTSA records that the vehicles have no permanently attached conventional manual controls, naming a brake pedal, a gas pedal, a steering wheel and mirrors.
claims.quote: The vehicles lack permanently attached, conventional manual controls, such as a brake pedal, gas pedal, steering wheel, and mirrors.
claims.document: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation, opening resume for Audit Query AQ26002

claims.text: NHTSA says it will consider how far Tesla's certification rested on determinations that certain standards do not apply to the Cybercab at all.
claims.quote: Among other things, NHTSA will consider the extent to which Tesla's certification depended on determinations that certain FMVSS are inapplicable to the Cybercab.
claims.document: NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation, opening resume for Audit Query AQ26002

claims.text: Reporting confirms the audit was opened the same day Tesla began carrying passengers in Austin.
claims.quote: NHTSA opened an audit into how Tesla certified the vehicle the same day the company started putting passengers in it in Austin.
claims.document: Electrek, Tesla Cybercab already under NHTSA investigation over FMVSS certification

claims.text: Reporting identifies the action as an Open Audit Query numbered AQ26002 from NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation.
claims.quote: The investigation is an Open Audit Query, numbered AQ26002, from NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation.
claims.document: Electrek, Tesla Cybercab already under NHTSA investigation over FMVSS certification

claims.text: Reporting independently gives the covered fleet as an estimated 1,000 Cybercab vehicles.
claims.quote: covers an estimated 1,000 Cybercab vehicles
claims.document: Electrek, Tesla Cybercab already under NHTSA investigation over FMVSS certification

claims.text: Many of the federal standards were written around a human driver and assume controls the driver can reach, none of which the Cybercab has.
claims.quote: They assume there's a steering wheel, a brake pedal, side mirrors, and controls the driver can reach. The Cybercab has none of those.
claims.document: Electrek, Tesla Cybercab already under NHTSA investigation over FMVSS certification

claims.text: NHTSA announced the probe on the Friday morning after Tesla put the first Cybercabs on Austin streets.
claims.quote: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) announced Friday morning that it opened the probe mere hours after Tesla put the first Cybercabs on the streets of Austin, Texas.
claims.document: TechCrunch, Feds launch investigation into Tesla's Cybercab deployment

claims.text: NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison said the agency supports automated vehicles and has to ensure the laws are followed.
claims.quote: NHTSA fully supports the safe development and deployment of automated vehicles. But as the federal regulator, we need to ensure that all of our laws are followed.
claims.document: TechCrunch, Feds launch investigation into Tesla's Cybercab deployment

claims.text: Federal rules require manual controls such as brake pedals, and the Department of Transportation has recently proposed removing that requirement for vehicles designed to drive themselves.
claims.quote: Federal vehicle safety regulations require manual controls like brake pedals, though the Department of Transportation recently proposed removing those requirements for vehicles that are designed to be autonomously driven.
claims.document: TechCrunch, Feds launch investigation into Tesla's Cybercab deployment

claims.text: NHTSA says the standards on manual controls are being rewritten, and that until the work is finished the existing standards still apply.
claims.quote: Until that work is completed, however, existing standards remain in force.
claims.document: TechCrunch, Feds launch investigation into Tesla's Cybercab deployment

claims.text: Zoox self-certified its robotaxi in 2022, a vehicle that also lacks a steering wheel and pedals.
claims.quote: In 2022, Amazon-owned autonomous vehicle company Zoox self-certified its cube-like robotaxi, which lacks traditional controls such as a steering wheel and pedals.
claims.document: TechCrunch, Feds launch investigation into Tesla's Cybercab deployment

claims.text: Zoox later filed for a temporary Part 555 exemption from eight Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards so it could charge for rides.
claims.quote: Zoox then went through the official process and filed for a temporary Part 555 exemption from eight Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards in hopes it would get the final OK that would allow it to charge for robotaxi rides.
claims.document: TechCrunch, Feds launch investigation into Tesla's Cybercab deployment

claims.text: Zoox received final approval for that exemption in July 2026.
claims.quote: Zoox received final approval for that exemption in July 2026, eliminating one of the last remaining regulatory hurdles the company needed to clear before launching a commercial robotaxi service.
claims.document: TechCrunch, Feds launch investigation into Tesla's Cybercab deployment

claims.text: Part 555 is the rule under which NHTSA grants a temporary exemption from one or more federal motor vehicle safety standards.
claims.quote: This part establishes requirements for the temporary exemption by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) of certain motor vehicles from compliance with one or more Federal motor vehicle safety standards
claims.document: 49 CFR 555.1, Purpose and scope, Cornell Legal Information Institute

claims.text: Any interested person may petition NHTSA's Administrator to start a proceeding on whether a motor vehicle fails to comply with an applicable federal motor vehicle safety standard.
claims.quote: Any interested person may file with the Administrator a petition requesting him: (a) To commence a proceeding respecting the issuance, amendment or revocation of a motor vehicle safety standard, or (b) To commence a proceeding to decide whether to issue an order concerning the notification and remedy of a failure of a motor vehicle or item of replacement equipment to comply with an applicable motor vehicle safety standard or a defect in such vehicle or equipment that relates to motor vehicle safety.
claims.document: 49 CFR 552.3, Filing of petitions, Cornell Legal Information Institute
claims.why: THE DECK HAD NO DOOR AND THE RECORD SAID IT DID. tx-2026-0140's public_access.how reads that a member of the public can read the resume and file a vehicle safety complaint with the same office, and no claim in this file carried any public route, so no frame could print one without inventing it. nhtsa.gov returns 403 to this run's fetcher on every page, the AQ26002 resume carries no complaint boilerplate, and a search snippet is not a fetched source. 49 CFR 552.3 is fetchable, primary, and is a NARROWER and better door than a complaint: it is the rule under which a person asks the agency to decide whether a vehicle meets an applicable standard, which is this deck's exact subject.

rejected.finding: Zoox took the Part 555 route instead of self-certifying, which is how the showrunner framed it in the brief
rejected.reason: Contradicted by the source. Zoox DID self-certify, in 2022, was investigated for it, and only then filed for Part 555. The two routes were sequential, not alternative. Any slide saying Zoox chose an exemption instead of self-certifying is false.

rejected.finding: Under its exemption Zoox may add 2,500 vehicles per year over two years
rejected.reason: The only string carrying 2,500 came back internally garbled and a second fetch did not return it again. A numeral this project publishes must come from a quote known to be verbatim. Dropped.

rejected.finding: NHTSA press release on Cybercab self-certification
rejected.reason: HTTP 403 to the fact-checker as well as to the earlier fetcher, body never retrieved. Nothing from it is in the record.

rejected.finding: Text of 49 CFR Part 555 from eCFR
rejected.reason: ecfr.gov returned 302 to a bot wall. Cornell's republication of 49 CFR 555.1 stands in for c23. The eCFR itself was never read.

rejected.finding: Direct reading of the AQ26002 PDF by the fact-checker
rejected.reason: The PDF text layer could not be read by the checking tools. Claims c1 to c11 rest on the showrunner's pypdf extraction of a file fetched at HTTP 200. SIX of the eleven are independently corroborated by Electrek or TechCrunch and carry high confidence: c1 and c3 by c13, c2 and c7 by c12 and c16, c5 by c14, c10 by c15. FIVE are not: c4, c6, c8, c9 and c11 appear in the extraction and nowhere else. c8 and c9 are the two quote plates the deck prints on slides 3 and 8, so the deck's two longest quotations rest on one uncorroborated extraction of a primary document. Stated here rather than left to be counted. CORRECTED 2026-09-10: this reason said eight and the file records six, which the round 3 integrity judge found by counting them.

rejected.finding: The investigator, reviewer and approver names on the resume
rejected.reason: They appear only in the uncorroborated extraction, they name private individuals, and they carry no editorial weight for a deck about certification process. Excluded deliberately rather than for failure.

rejected.finding: Any claim about Cybercab driving behaviour, safety record or crashes
rejected.reason: None found in any fetched source and none would be admitted. AQ26002 audits certification paperwork rather than a defect. The deck must not imply a safety finding exists.

rejected.finding: The reporter's line that the 2022 Zoox investigation did slow its path to commercialization
rejected.reason: Verbatim in the source, but it is a characterisation of an outcome rather than a documented decision, and it invites a predictive read of what AQ26002 will do to Tesla. Out on editorial grounds.

rejected.finding: Slide 2's SUBJECT row printed a string no claim carried
rejected.reason: FOUND BY THE INTEGRITY JUDGE IN ROUND 1. The string is verbatim in the resume this run fetched, and it was briefly admitted as c24. The SUBJECT row then came off the frame in the same round to pay for the negation row against the 65 word ceiling, which left c24 on no frame and in no source list. A claim nothing cites is not evidence, it is furniture, so it was withdrawn with the row.
